title: Lane ships skip golangci-lint, so lint debt reaches main and then blocks every console commit to that package
summary: The local commit gate (internal/commitgate/lanes.go laneGo) runs golangci-lint over every package a change touches. Lane ships do not run it, and neither does CI (go/.golangci.yml says CI enforces vet+gofmt+tests only). On 2026-09-26 origin/main carried two production findings: errcheck on `defer f.Close()` at internal/dossier/read.go (added by cycle commit f3044a3b), and staticcheck QF1001 at internal/faillearn/novelty.go. A comment-only console batch on internal/dossier could not pass its commit gate, because a comment-only change may not fix code. The console fix is branch fix/production-lint-debt. Until the class is fixed, debt can come back with any lane.
fix: Put one lint check in the lane path, the same golangci-lint config over the changed packages, as a composed ship or build-exit gate. It must share the commit gate's implementation, not copy it. Roll it out shadow → enforce through the stage config, the way the other gates do. Another option is to make the commit gate lint only new issues (--new-from-rev), but that lets debt pile up with nothing noticing, so only consider it alongside the lane gate.
acceptance: A lane change that adds a golangci-lint finding in production code is flagged before it reaches main (shadow WARN with a coded signal, then correction)
The lane check and the commit gate share one lint implementation and one config
A test proves a lane build with an unchecked Close error is caught
priority_rationale: inbox review 2026-09-27: Lane lint debt blocks console commits (seen 2026-09-26). It is two standards for one tree, not a loop-stability defect.
